Level 1 · Introduction

Cheat Sheet

Scratch blocks (weeks 1--6) and Python turtle (weeks 7--12)

Print it (PDF, 66 KB) Dyslexia-friendly edition (PDF)

Scratch blocks

 Events

Start the code. Message names must match!

 Motion

nn sides: turn 360÷n360 \div n. The middle is (0, 0).

 Looks &  Pen

Costumes in a loop = animation. Pen: Extension button.

 Control

Loops repeat what is inside. if: only when true. else: when false.

 Ask, variables, random

The reply goes into answer. A variable is a labeled box.

 My Blocks

Make a Block with a name and inputs, then use it.

Python turtle in Thonny

Getting started

import turtle Load the turtle tools.
t = turtle.Turtle() Make a turtle: t.
screen = turtle.Screen() The window.
turtle.done() Keep it open (last line).

Moving and drawing

t.forward(100) Walk 100 steps.
t.back(50) Walk backwards.
t.left(90) Turn left 90 degrees.
t.right(90) Turn right 90 degrees.
t.penup() Pen up: move, no line.
t.pendown() Pen down: draw again.
t.goto(x, y) Jump to (x,y)(x, y).
t.setheading(90) Face up (0 = right).
t.circle(50) Circle, radius 50.
t.dot(20, YELLOW) A filled dot.
t.write("Hi!") Write on the picture.

Colors and style

t.color("#0072B2") Pen and fill color.
t.color(BLACK, ORANGE) Lines, then fill.
t.begin_fill() Start coloring in…
t.end_fill() … fill it now!
t.pensize(3) Thicker lines.
t.speed(0) Fastest drawing.
t.hideturtle() Hide the arrow.
screen.bgcolor(BLACK) Background color.

Color-blind-safe colors

ORANGE #E69F00 SKY_BLUE #56B4E9
GREEN #009E73 YELLOW #F0E442
BLUE #0072B2 VERMILLION #D55E00
PURPLE #CC79A7 BLACK #000000

Thonny keys

Run F5 Stop Cmd+F2 Save Cmd+S Bigger text Cmd++

Python words

print("Hello") Show text in the Shell.
# a comment A note for humans.
size = 50 A variable (labeled box).
answer = input("Size? ") Ask. The answer is text.
n = int(answer) Text to a number.
import random Load the surprises.
random.randint(1, 6) Random: 1 to 6.

Loops, choices and functions

for i in range(4):   # repeat 4 times
    t.forward(100)   # inside the loop
    t.left(90)

if n > 10:
    print("Lots!")
elif n == 10:
    print("Exactly ten")
else:
    print("A few")

def square(size):    # make a command
    for i in range(4):
        t.forward(size)
        t.left(90)

square(50)           # use it!

Compare: > bigger, < smaller, == equal, != not equal.

Python is picky!

  • Small letters: print, not Print.

  • A colon : ends every for, if, else, def line.

  • Lines inside are pushed in 4 spaces (Tab).

  • Every ( needs a ); every " needs a partner.

  • Never name a file turtle.py or random.py.
